endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Acceptance decisions should be time-bound and subject to re-evaluation at defined intervals or when material changes occur.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: The implementer team should be aware of any effect that changes to architecture and code have to the level of risk, and there should be processes in place to manage risk arising from changes to system, environment, and data.

endorsements.title: Integrating enterprise risk management to address AI-related risks in healthcare: Strategies for effective risk mitigation and implementation
endorsements.issuer: Journal of healthcare risk management : the journal of the American Society for Healthcare Risk Management
endorsements.quote: ERM is not a static process but a dynamic one, necessitating continuous evaluation of the effectiveness of risk control measures and updating the risk management plan based on new information and technological advancements.

endorsements.title: When Is It Safe to Introduce an AI System Into Healthcare? A Practical Decision Algorithm for the Ethical Implementation of Black-Box AI in Medicine
endorsements.quote: All risk categories require a process of regular monitoring and iterative review.

endorsements.title: ONRAMP-AI-VRAR: an operational protocol for ethics and governance of AI-enabled immersive psychotherapy
endorsements.quote: Re-score quarterly and after material changes; escalate tier if risk, autonomy, scale, or sensitivity rises,

endorsements.title: Governing Patient-Facing AI-Generated Video in Digital Health: A Risk-and-Ethics Matrix for Deployment, Monitoring, and Change Control
endorsements.quote: Because both risk and ethics are provisional in fast-moving sociotechnical contexts [ 40 ], institutions should version scores with date-stamped assumptions and require rereview after model updates, distribution channel changes, or sentinel events.

commentary.bottom_line: Six sources, all frameworks or commentaries, endorse periodic and change-triggered reassessment of AI risk, but no study tests whether the practice keeps risk assessments current or prevents harm. No study was supplied that documents stale risk assessments as a measured problem in health care AI.

perspectives.view: No study tests reassessment on a cadence or after material change, and no study documents the hazard. The six endorsements consist of two CHAI frameworks and four commentaries. They agree on the principle, but agreement among expert opinion sources does not raise GRADE certainty. The recommendation therefore rests on consensus rather than measured effect.

The endorsements name model updates, distribution channel changes, and sentinel events as triggers for re-review. These triggers are plausible failure points, but no supplied study shows how often assessments go stale or whether re-review catches problems before they reach patients.

One commentary proposes quarterly re-scoring, and another asks institutions to version scores with date-stamped assumptions. No source reports the staff time, cost, or completion rates of such schedules, so health systems have no evidence to size the workload or choose an interval.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare scheduled and change-triggered reassessment with one-time assessment. These studies should measure how often reassessments detect changed risk, whether they lead to mitigation or withdrawal, the staff effort involved, and downstream patient harm. Descriptive work that measures how often deployed AI risk assessments become outdated would also establish whether the hazard occurs in practice.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Reassessment triggers named in the endorsements do not mention shifts in the patient population served, so a system may not detect risk changes that arise when a tool expands to these groups.
